problem: Existing AudioGoal navigation agents act at a fixed granularity: either myopic step-by-step RL actions (Chen et al.) or a single final-goal prediction from audio (Gan et al.). Hierarchical visual-nav methods set subgoals with hand-designed heuristics (frontiers, shortest-path points), and audio is aggregated only with an unstructured GRU.
motivation: A distant sound source is hard to localize directly, but the general direction and a navigable path toward it are easier to identify. Audio gives the goal direction and vision gives obstacles and free space, so jointly learned intermediate waypoints and a spatially grounded record of heard audio should make navigation more efficient and robust to unheard sounds and noise.
key_idea: Learn end-to-end with RL a policy that dynamically sets audio-visual waypoints from a geometric map, an acoustic memory map and binaural audio, and execute each waypoint with an analytic shortest-path planner.
insight: Ablations show the waypoint policy is the biggest contributor: replacing it with primitive actions drops Matterport heard SPL from 72.3 to 44.3. Even without the maps, the waypoint framework beats Chen et al. The acoustic memory matters most for unheard sounds and noise; on Matterport unheard, removing A_t and G_t lowers SPL from 40.9 to 20.5. Learned waypoints also beat frontier, direction-following and supervised waypoints, which suggests supervision defines the optimal waypoint too narrowly. Learned waypoints cluster at doors and obstacles and are longer when the agent is far from the goal.
method: Geometric map G_t: back-projects depth to a 2D egocentric occupancy/explored map (3x3 m local) and fuses it into an allocentric map by averaging.
Acoustic memory A_t: a ground-plane map holding a moving average of direct-sound intensity at visited positions, giving structured, interpretable distance/direction cues.
Encoders + GRU: CNN encoders f_g, f_b, f_a produce 512-d features for the maps and binaural spectrogram; they are concatenated and fed to a GRU.
Waypoint actor-critic: outputs a distribution over a 9x9 action map of relative waypoints, masked by the local occupancy map; waypoint (0,0) means Stop.
Path planner: Dijkstra on G_t (unexplored treated as free) turns each waypoint into low-level actions, with a 10-step planning limit and a random action if no path is found.

Reward and training: +10 for success, +0.25 for geodesic distance reduction (equal penalty for increase), -0.01 per action; the waypoint reward is the cumulative reward from the planner round; trained with PPO, all modules jointly.

setting.backbone: CNN encoders + GRU actor-critic (trained from scratch with PPO) plus analytic Dijkstra planner
setting.training_data: SoundSpaces audio on Replica (9 train scenes) and Matterport3D (73 train scenes); heard = telephone sound, unheard = disjoint split of 102 sounds; 7.5M policy steps
setting.observation: egocentric depth + binaural audio spectrograms (no GPS/goal vector)
setting.action_space: predicted waypoints on a 9x9 local grid (0.5 m Replica / 1 m Matterport grid) executed via low-level MoveForward/TurnLeft/TurnRight/Stop
setting.privileged: none (the agent's pose/odometry is used for map registration)

numbers_note: Split labelled 'test' because tables report performance on unseen test scenes (the paper does not name the split explicitly). Distractor-sound results are in text only (Replica SPL 83.1, Matterport SPL 70.9); the microphone-noise results are shown only in a figure.
results: AV-WaN beats all baselines on heard sounds: SPL gains over Chen et al. of 8.4 on Replica (86.6 vs 78.2) and 17.2 on Matterport (72.3 vs 55.1), and over Gan et al. of 29 and 49.5. On unheard sounds it is best on Matterport (SPL 40.9 vs 25.9) and ties Chen et al. on Replica SPL (34.7 vs 34.7 in the table, though the text claims 2.8 lower), while leading on SNA. It is also more robust to distractor and microphone noise.
limitations: Evaluated only in simulation on a discrete 0.5 m/1 m audio grid, so noisy actuation could not be tested and there is no real-robot transfer
Failure cases: oscillation around goals cornered near walls due to reflections or mapping errors, and premature Stop near the goal
Unheard-sound performance is still far below heard-sound performance, and only static single sound sources are handled
builds_on: Gan et al. 2019 (Look, Listen, and Act)
